items.stem: Which transformation maps y = cos x onto y = cos(3x)?
items.markingKey: A horizontal stretch, scale factor 1/3. Replacing x by 3x compresses horizontally by factor 1/3.

items.stem: Rafael writes: "The amplitude of y = −4cos x + 1 is −4." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Amplitude is a distance, so it is |−4| = 4.
items.markingKey: Amplitude is a distance, so it is |−4| = 4. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Describe a sequence of transformations that maps the graph of y = sin x onto the graph of y = 3sin(4(x − π/6)) + 1, explaining the effect of each parameter.
items.answer: horizontal stretch scale factor 1/4 (period becomes π/2); translation of π/6 to the right; vertical stretch scale factor 3; translation of 1 up
items.markingKey: A1 for each correct transformation with its parameter (order: horizontal stretch before the horizontal translation of c, which is applied to x − c); R1 for explaining the effect on period/amplitude/axis. horizontal stretch scale factor 1/4 (period becomes π/2); translation of π/6 to the right; vertical stretch scale factor 3; translation of 1 up

items.stem: The graph of y = a cos(b(x − c)) + d, with a, b > 0 and the smallest possible c ≥ 0, has a maximum point at (4, 12) and the next minimum point at (10, −1). Find the values of a, b, c and d.
items.markingKey: a = (12 − (−1))/2 = 13/2 A1; d = (12 + (−1))/2 = 11/2 A1; period = 2 × 6 = 12 (M1) so b = 2π/12 = π/6 A1; cosine has its maximum where b(x − c) = 0, so c = 4 A1.

items.stem: Let f(x) = 8cos(2(x − π/3)) − 2, x ≥ 0. Find the coordinates of the first maximum point and of the first minimum point of the graph of f.
items.markingKey: Max value −2 + 8 = 6, min value −10 (A1 A1); cos is maximal when its argument is 0 (+2πn) (M1); x = π/3 (A1); minimum half a period (π/2) away: x = 5π/6 (A1).

The mean monthly temperature T (°C) in Mumbai is modelled by T(t) = a cos(b(t − c)) + d, where t is the time in months after the start of the year (t = 1 is mid-January). The highest mean temperature, 29 °C, occurs at t = 1; the lowest, 13 °C, occurs six months later.
(a) Find the values of a, b, c and d (b > 0, a > 0).
(b) Use the model to estimate T at t = 10.5.

items.answer: (a) a = 8, b = π/6 ≈ 0.524, c = 1, d = 21 (b) 23.1 °C (c) 6.00 months (d) e.g. real temperatures are not exactly sinusoidal / vary year to year
items.markingKey: (a) a = (29 − 13)/2 A1, d = (29 + 13)/2 A1, period 12 so b = 2π/12 (M1) A1, c = 1 A1. (b) substitution (M1) 23.1 A1. (c) solve T(t) = 21 with GDC: t = 4.00, 10.0 (A1); length 6.00 months A1. (d) R1 for a sensible limitation.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "phase shift"?
options: The horizontal line y = d about which a sinusoidal graph oscillates, midway between its maximum and minimum
The set of all solutions of a trigonometric equation, e.g. x = π/6 + 2πn or x = 5π/6 + 2πn for sin x = 1/2
The horizontal translation c in y = a sin(b(x − c)) + d
The single solution of a trigonometric equation returned by the inverse function (arcsin, arccos, arctan), lying in its restricted range
items.answer: The horizontal translation c in y = a sin(b(x − c)) + d
items.markingKey: C. "phase shift" is the horizontal translation c in y = a sin(b(x − c)) + d.

items.stem: Consider f(x) = 4cos(x/3) − 3. What is the range of the graph of f?
items.markingKey: D. For a sin(b(x − c)) + d: amplitude |a| = 4, period 2π/b = 6π, principal axis y = −3, range [−7, 1].

items.stem: Outline the meaning of the term "amplitude".
items.answer: Half the distance between the maximum and minimum values of a sinusoidal function; for y = a sin(b(x − c)) + d it is |a|
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: half the distance between the maximum and minimum values of a sinusoidal function; for y = a sin(b(x − c)) + d it is |a|. Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: Explain why the period of y = sin(bx) is 2π/b for b > 0.
items.answer: sin repeats when its argument increases by 2π; bx increases by 2π when x increases by 2π/b.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: sin repeats when its argument increases by 2π; bx increases by 2π when x increases by 2π/b. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain why the principal axis of a sinusoidal graph is midway between the maximum and minimum.
items.answer: The function is d + a·(sine), and the sine part takes values symmetrically in [−1, 1], so values range from d − |a| to d + |a| with d in the middle.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: The function is d + a·(sine), and the sine part takes values symmetrically in [−1, 1], so values range from d − |a| to d + |a| with d in the middle. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: "The period of y = sin(2x) is 4π because the 2 doubles the period." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Multiplying x by 2 halves the period: 2π/2 = π.
items.markingKey: Multiplying x by 2 halves the period: 2π/2 = π. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Lars solves sin x cos x = (√2/2) sin x for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π by dividing both sides by sin x, and obtains x = π/4, 7π/4. Explain why this is incomplete and give the complete solution set.

items.stem: Explain why the equation 4 cos x = 5 has no real solutions.

items.stem: The function f(t) = 7 sin((2π/24)t) + 13 models the number of visitors (hundreds) to a ski resort, where t is measured in weeks after 1 January. Explain the meaning of each of the numbers 7, 24 and 13 in this context.
items.answer: 7: amplitude (maximum variation from the mean); 24: period (one full cycle takes 24 units of t); 13: mean / principal axis value.
items.markingKey: Amplitude 7: the quantity rises and falls 7 above and below its mean (R1); period 24: the pattern repeats every 24 weeks (R1); 13: the mean level, midway between max 20 and min 6 (R1).

Which of the following best describes "periodic model"?
options: The horizontal translation c in y = a sin(b(x − c)) + d
A function that repeats at regular intervals, used for phenomena such as tides, daylight hours and rotating wheels
A function of the form y = a sin(b(x − c)) + d or y = a cos(b(x − c)) + d used to model periodic behaviour
The single solution of a trigonometric equation returned by the inverse function (arcsin, arccos, arctan), lying in its restricted range
items.answer: A function that repeats at regular intervals, used for phenomena such as tides, daylight hours and rotating wheels
items.markingKey: B. "periodic model" is a function that repeats at regular intervals, used for phenomena such as tides, daylight hours and rotating wheels.

items.stem: Chloé solves sin x cos x = (√3/2) sin x for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π by dividing both sides by sin x, and obtains x = π/6, 11π/6. Explain why this is incomplete and give the complete solution set.
items.markingKey: Dividing by sin x assumes sin x ≠ 0 (R1); factorise: sin x (cos x − (√3/2)) = 0 (M1); sin x = 0 gives x = 0, π, 2π (A1); complete set 0, π/6, π, 11π/6, 2π (A1).

items.stem: Explain why a negative value of a in y = a sin x reflects the graph in the x-axis.
items.answer: Each y-value is multiplied by a negative number, so positive values become negative and vice versa, which is a reflection in the x-axis (combined with a stretch of |a|).
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Each y-value is multiplied by a negative number, so positive values become negative and vice versa, which is a reflection in the x-axis (combined with a stretch of |a|). items.stem: Explain why the equation sin²x + sin x + 3 = 0 has no real solutions.
items.answer: The discriminant is negative (or roots outside [−1, 1]).
items.markingKey: As a quadratic in sin x: discriminant 1² − 4(3) = −11 < 0 (M1 A1), so there is no real value of sin x and hence no solution (R1).

items.stem:
